questions.q: What's the recommended catalog structure for a real organization?
options: One catalog per environment (dev/staging/prod), with consistent schemas underneath, rather than one catalog per project or team
One catalog per individual user
A single catalog for the entire organization with no further structure
One catalog per table, regardless of environment
questions.explain: Per-project catalogs fragment the namespace and make environment promotion much harder to reason about.

questions.q: Why is granting access to a group preferred over granting to individual users?
options: Access naturally follows role changes — someone joining or leaving a group updates their access automatically, with zero grants needing to be touched
Group grants and individual grants behave completely differently under Unity Catalog
Individual grants are always more secure than group grants
Groups can only be used with Delta Sharing, not regular GRANT statements
questions.explain: Individual grants require someone to remember to clean them up when a person's role changes.

questions.q: How does the dev/staging/prod catalog pattern relate to Lesson 39?
options: It's the real best-practice application of Lesson 39's point that the same schema.table names can exist safely in different catalogs
It contradicts what Lesson 39 taught about catalogs
It requires abandoning the three-level namespace entirely
Lesson 39 only applies to single-catalog setups
questions.explain: dev.bronze.trips and prod.bronze.trips sharing the same schema.table names is exactly this pattern.

questions.q: What does Chapter 5 (Lakeflow) address that's still missing after Chapter 4?
options: A unified, coherent system for orchestrating ingestion, pipelines, and jobs, rather than separately-managed pieces
Access control, which hasn't been covered at all yet
The three-level namespace, which Chapter 4 never actually explained
Delta Lake's transaction log, which Chapter 4 replaces
questions.explain: Everything in this course is still ingested and transformed through notebooks and manually-scheduled jobs.

questions.q: Does GRANT's syntax differ between granting to a group versus an individual user?
options: No — Lesson 42's GRANT syntax works identically either way; the durability difference comes from what's granted to, not how
Yes, groups require a completely different SQL command
Yes, only individual users can be granted SELECT, never groups
Group grants require Delta Sharing specifically
questions.explain: The syntax is the same — the real difference is the long-term durability of who the grant targets.
